summary: Tatsugen Sato was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed a doctorate at Komazawa University in 1978. He served at Komazawa University as assistant professor (~1968–1995) and professor (~1978–1995), and taught at Ryukoku and Tokai universities.
Tatsuhiro Saito is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996). He founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.

Tatsuo Hayashi was a philosopher and historian who studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1921). He held academic posts at Hosei University (~1925–1932) and Meiji University (~1946–1957), as well as Toyo, Tsuda, and Rikkyo universities.

Tatsuo Nishida was a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology who earned a doctorate at Kyoto University, later serving there as professor and dean. He also held posts at the National Center for Science Information Systems and the Japan Academy.

Tatyana Elizarenkova was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Mikhaïl Peterson at Moscow State University (~1946–1951). She spent her career at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1957–2007).

Tavivat Puntarigvivat works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, holding an M.A. from the University of Hawaiʻi and studying under Luangpor Teean Jittasubho. He held positions at Mahidol University, Kyoto University, and the World Buddhist University.
Taw Sein Ko was a scholar of archaeology, history, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Rangoon (~1879–1881), the Inner Temple (~1892–1893), and the Inns of Court (~1892–1893).

Teizo Iyanaga was a scholar of Japanese history and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1935–1938). He held academic posts at Nagoya University (~1949–1956), the University of Tokyo (~1956–1976), and Sophia University (~1976–1983).
Tej Ram Sharma is an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist who earned a doctorate at Banaras Hindu University in 1968. He held an academic post at Himachal Pradesh University around 1974.
Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Lobsang Gyatso, and also taught Lobsang Gyatso.

Tenga Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar who studied at Benchen Monastery and under Situ Rinpoche. He served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery (~1967–1980) and founded Benchen Monastery in 1976.

Tensei Kitabatake was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1950–1955), where he later served as professor and president (1995–1999). He was subsequently president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005).
Tenshin Tanouye was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Sogen Omori. He founded Chozen-ji.
Tenzin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Hanna Havnevik and completed a Master of Philosophy at the University of Oslo (attested 2008).

Tenzin Dorjee is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Geshes Lobsang Tsephel, Sonam Rinchen, and Dawa. He worked as a translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and at Pullahari Monastery (attested 2000).

Tenzin Gyatso is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under teachers including Trijang Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse. He founded the International Network of Engaged Buddhists in 1989 and taught numerous scholars.

Tenzin Gyatso, 14th Dalai Lama, is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Reting Rinpoche, Taktra Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and Trijang Rinpoche, and has taught scholars including Jeffrey Hopkins and Robert A. F. Thurman.

Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who earned a Geshe degree at Menri Monastery. He directed the Dialectic School of Menri Monastery, served at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and founded Ligmincha International.

Ter Ellingson is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1979). He served on the faculty at the University of Washington (1981–2016).

Terese Tse Bartholomew is a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and archaeology who earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles. She served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco.
